sources.publisher: Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife
sources.scope: 09-137 CMR Chapter 24, Licensed Guides. Defines guide, inland waters, and territorial waters. Classifications: specialized hunting; specialized fishing on inland waters; specialized recreational, including inland paddlesports; specialized sea-kayaking on territorial seas; specialized tide-water fishing on territorial waters to the three-mile limit, except species harvested under a Department of Marine Resources license, and the rule does not apply aboard a vessel with a current U.S. Coast Guard certificate of inspection. A note requires a U.S. Coast Guard license to carry passengers for hire when operating a motorboat on territorial seas and tributaries to guide hunting or fishing. Master certification is an experience overlay. Substantive amendments on the file run through filing 2021-072 on April 13, 2021, with an APAO accessibility check dated July 30, 2025. No roster and no data dictionary of license fields.
sources.access: Public Word download opened and extracted on the check date
sources.rights_basis: Rule text states who must hold which classification. It does not grant directory reuse of the licensee file.
sources.bulk: single chapter file; not a licensee extract

sources.publisher: Maine Office of the Revisor of Statutes
sources.scope: 12 M.R.S. §12853. A person may not act as a guide without a valid license, with narrow youth-camp and educational-trip exceptions. Applicant must be at least 18, pass the examination, meet first-aid and rule requirements, and submit to a state and FBI background check. Background-check results are confidential. Fee is $135. License expires December 31 of the fourth complete year after issuance. Page data extracted 2026-10-05.
sources.rights_basis: Official unannotated statute. The page says the Revisor does not provide legal advice. It does not state a commercial-directory license. Confidentiality of background-check results is explicit. Confidentiality of the license record itself is in §10111.

sources.publisher: Maine Office of the Revisor of Statutes
sources.role: MDIFW license-record confidentiality and disclosure statute
sources.scope: 12 M.R.S. §10111, enacted by PL 2025, c. 692. Personally identifiable information in department license, permit, registration, harvest, and application records is confidential, including telephone, email, physical address, online licensing ID, date of birth, driver's license number, Social Security number, and taxpayer ID. For a commercial record, telephone, email, and physical address are not treated as personally identifiable information. The department may disseminate data that is not personally identifiable and may include names and mailing addresses from licenses. It may charge reasonable fees for individual records or whole or partial databases, outside the fee limits of 1 M.R.S. §408-A. Confidential PII remains confidential for 100 years. Statute page extracted 2026-10-05. The second regular session law volume states a general effective date of July 29, 2026 for nonemergency laws, and this section shows no separate emergency clause.
sources.credential_holder: the department holds the records; the license is issued to an individual
sources.access: Public statute page. No public database is linked from the section.
sources.rights_basis: Disclosure of non-PII data, including names and mailing addresses, is something the department may do. The statute does not require a public roster, does not grant a third party the right to republish a commercial directory, and is silent on attribution and downstream redistribution.
sources.bulk: whole or partial database copies are authorized at a reasonable fee if the department furnishes them; no public bulk file was found
sources.request_process: No dedicated online permission form was found. A request would go to MDIFW. Fees for these database copies are not capped by the Freedom of Access Act fee rules. A FOAA request remains available for records that are public, with the confidentiality exceptions in this section.

sources.publisher: Maine Office of the Revisor of Statutes
sources.scope: 1 M.R.S. §408-A. Right to inspect and copy public records within a reasonable time, with acknowledgment in 5 working days, copy and staff-time fees, electronic format rules, and a fee waiver when release is in the public interest and is not primarily in the requester's commercial interest. Page extracted 2026-10-05.
sources.rights_basis: The statute governs inspection and copying. It does not grant a license to build a commercial directory from records that another statute makes confidential. The commercial-interest clause is a fee-waiver test, not a reuse grant. For MDIFW license databases, §10111 expressly removes those copies from these fee limits.
sources.bulk: electronic copy of an existing public record, if confidential fields can be separated
sources.request_process: Request to the agency that holds the record. Writing is not required. The agency acknowledges within 5 working days and may require advance payment when the estimate exceeds $100.

sources.request_process: Copyright notices: Tyler Technologies, Chief Legal Officer, copyright@tylertech.com. That path is for infringement notices, not for permission to publish a directory.

sources.publisher: Maine Office of the Revisor of Statutes
sources.scope: 12 M.R.S. §6313. An individual needs a current for-hire charter boat operator's license to take paying passengers recreationally fishing in coastal waters, on the vessel identified on that license. The license does not authorize sale of the fish. No license fee; agent fees of $1 or $2 may apply. Eligibility, as amended by PL 2025, c. 570: a U.S. Coast Guard merchant mariner credential with an endorsement to carry passengers for hire, or a current tidewater fishing guide license under §12853. The prior eligibility path, a merchant marine document for an uninspected-passenger-vessel operator or a master or mate license, is repealed on the current compiled page. Enacted by PL 2025, c. 155, effective January 1, 2026. Chapter 570 carries the second-regular-session general effective date of July 29, 2026, and the compiled section extracted 2026-10-05 already contains the amendment. Civil violation, $100 to $500.
sources.credential_holder: individual; the license names one vessel
sources.access: Public statute page. The license file is not published here. Issuance is described by the department as its LEEDS licensing system.
sources.rights_basis: The statute creates the credential and ties it to a named vessel. It does not publish the roster and does not grant commercial reuse, redistribution, attribution, or bulk access.
sources.request_process: No public download. A records request would be a Department of Marine Resources FOAA or licensing-data request. Whether the vessel field is releasable was not decided on any page checked.

sources.scope: Free self-listings on VisitMaine.com for Maine businesses with a physical location that serve travelers. The business creates its own listing, MOT reviews it, and the contributor is told to review it at least annually. Contributors may post only their own businesses. sources.request_process: A business applies at the Visit Maine extranet form linked from this page. That process puts the business on Visit Maine. It does not authorize another directory to claim or republish the listing.
